title: Combine Employees and Contractors with UNION
description:
Combine two separate tables — employees and contractors — into a single list of all workers. Use `UNION` (which removes duplicate rows) rather than `UNION ALL`.

**Table: employees** — `id`, `name`, `role`
**Table: contractors** — `id`, `name`, `role`

Return `name` and `role` for everyone. Order by `name`.
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE employees (id INT, name VARCHAR, role VARCHAR); CREATE TABLE contractors (id INT, name VARCHAR, role VARCHAR); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (1,'Alice','Engineer'),(2,'Bob','Manager'),(3,'Carol','Designer'),(4,'Dave','Engineer'),(5,'Eve','Manager'); INSERT INTO contractors VALUES (1,'Frank','Engineer'),(2,'Grace','Designer'),(3,'Hank','Consultant'),(4,'Iris','Engineer');
solution_sql: SELECT name, role FROM employees UNION SELECT name, role FROM contractors ORDER BY name

test_cases.description: 9 distinct workers (5 employees + 4 contractors, no duplicate name-role pairs)

hints: UNION combines the result sets of two SELECT statements and removes duplicate rows.
Both SELECT statements must have the same number of columns in the same order.
Use UNION ALL if you want to keep duplicates (faster, no deduplication step).
explanation: UNION stacks the two SELECT results and removes duplicate (name, role) pairs. Since no employee and contractor share the same name and role, all 5 + 4 = 9 rows are retained. The ORDER BY clause at the end applies to the combined result.
